title: HW 4
text:
Suppose that \(X_{1} \dots X_n\) is an iid sample from \(U(0, \theta)\)

Find the limiting distribution of \(X_{(n)}\)
Find the limiting distribution of \(Y_{n} = n(\theta - X_{(n)})\)

title: HW 4
text:
sol

(a)
\[P(|X_{(n)}-\theta| > \epsilon) = P(X_{(n)} \leq \theta - \epsilon) = \left ( \frac {\theta - \epsilon}{\epsilon}\right )^{n} \to 0\]
\[\divideontimes\,\, X_{(n)} \xrightarrow{P} \theta\]


(b)
\[P(Y_n > y) =  P(n(\theta - X_{(n)}) >y) =  P(X_{(n)} > \theta - \frac yn) = \left (1 - \frac{y}{n\theta}\right )^{n} \to e^{-y/\theta}\]
\[P(Y_{n}  \geq y) \to 1 - e^{-y/\theta} \quad (y \geq 0)\]
\[Y_{n}  \sim \text{exp}(\lambda = 1/\theta), \quad \theta \to \infty\]

title: HW 4
text:
sol

(a)
step1
\[F(x)  = \int_{\mu}^{x} f(t) \,dt =   1-e^{-(x-\mu)}\]
\[P(X>x) = 1- F(x) =e^{-(x-\mu)}\]
step2
\[P(X_{(1)}>x) =  P(X_{1}>x,\dots X_{n}>x)\]
\[P(X_{(1)}>x) =  \{P(X>x)\}^{n} = e^{-n(x-\mu)}\]
\[F_{X_{(1)}}(x) = 1-P(X_{(1)}>x) = 1-e^{-n(x-\mu)}\]
step3
\[\divideontimes \,\,f_{x_{(1)}}(x) = \frac{d}{dx} F_{x_{(1)}}(x) = ne^{-n(x-\mu)}\]


(b)
\[P(|X_{(1)} - \mu| > \epsilon) = P(X_{(1)}> \mu + \epsilon) = e^{-nx}\]
\[n\to \infty,\,\, e^{-nx} \to 0\]
\[\divideontimes\,\, P(|X_{(1)} - \mu| > \epsilon) = P(X_{(1)}> \mu + \epsilon) = e^{-nx} \to 0\]
\[\divideontimes\,\, X_{(1)} \xrightarrow{P} \mu\]

title: HW 4
text:
sol

(a)
step1
\[F(x) = 1-\left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^\beta\]
\[P(X_{(1)}>x) = \{ P(X>x)\}^n = (1-F(x))^{n} = \left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^{n\beta } \]
step2
\[F_{X_{(1)}}(x) = P(X_{(1)} \leq x) = 1- P(X_{(1)} > x) \begin{cases} 0, \quad x\leq \alpha \\ \\
                                                                        1- \left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^{n\beta }, \quad x>\alpha. \end{cases}\]
step3
\(x>\alpha\)에서
\[f_{X_{(1)}}(x) = \frac{d}{dx}\,\,\left [  1- \left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^{n\beta }\right ] = n\beta \alpha^{n\beta}x^{-(n\beta + 1)} \]
\[\divideontimes \,\, f_{x_{(1)}} (x) = \frac { n\beta \alpha^{n\beta}}{x^{n\beta + 1}}, \quad X_{(1)} \sim \text{Pareto}(\alpha, n\beta)\]


(b)
\[F(x) = 1-\left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^\beta\]
이므로
\[F_{X_{n}}(x) = P(X_1 \leq x\dots X_n \leq x) = \{ P(X\leq x)\}^{n} = [F(x)]^{n}\]
따라서
\[F_{X_{(n)}} (x) = \left [ 1-\left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^\beta \right ]^{n}, \quad x > \alpha\]



(c)
\[F_{X_{(n)}} (x) = \left [ 1-\left( \frac{\alpha}{x}\right)^\beta \right ]^{n}, \quad x > \alpha\]
이므로
\[F_{X_{(n)}} (b_{n}x) = \left [ 1-\left( \frac{\alpha}{b_{n}x}\right)^\beta \right ]^{n}, \quad x > \alpha\]
그런데
\[\left( \frac{\alpha}{b_{n}x}\right)^\beta =  \frac{1}{n^{x\beta}}\]
따라서
\[F_{X_{(n)}} (b_{n}x) = \left [ 1-\frac{1}{n^{x\beta}} \right ]^{n}, \quad x > \alpha\]
\[\lim_{n\to\infty} F_{X_{(n)}}(b_n x)=\begin{cases}0, & x \le 0,\\[4pt] \exp\!\left(-x^{-\beta}\right), & x>0. \end{cases}\]
Frechet 분포를 따른다.

\(P(E_{7})\)은 두 개의 주사위 합이 7인 경우 이므로 \(\to\) (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1)

\(P(F)\)은 첫번째 주사위가 4가 나올 확률이므로

\[P(F) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}\]

\(P(T)\)은 두번째 주사위가 3가 나올 확률이므로

2 Pairwise indep check

\(E_{7}, F\): 두 개의 주사위 합이 7이면서, 첫 번째 주사위가 4가 나올 확률

\[\therefore \,\,P(E_{7} \cap F) = \frac{1}{36} = P(E_{7}) \times P(F)\]

이 이후에 pairwise도 1/36로 동일하며 pairwise indep를 보임.

3 \(P(E_{7}\cap F \cap T) = P(E_7)P(F)P(T)\)?

\(P(E_{7}\cap F \cap T)\): 두 주사위의 합이 7이면서, 첫번째 주사위의 눈이 4 두번째 주사위의 눈이 3일 확률.

\[\therefore \,\, P(E_{7}\cap F \cap T) = \frac{1}{36}\]

but….. \(P(E_7)P(F)P(T) = (\frac{1}{6})^{3} = \frac{1}{216}\)

\[\therefore \,\, P(E_{7}\cap F \cap T) \neq P(E_7)P(F)P(T)\]

title: HW 2
text:
sol
step1
n이 매우 크고, p가 매우 작으며, \(\lambda = np\)가 적잗한 크기일 떄, 포아송 근사를 만족
\[n = 100,000, \,\, p = 0.00002\]
\[\lambda = np = 2\]
step2
\[10 < X < 20 \to X \in \{11,12\dots 19\}\]
step3
\(Y \sim \text{POI}(2)\)
\[P(Y = k) = e^{-2} \frac{2^{k}}{k!}\]
step4
\[P(10<X<20)  \approx \sum_{k=11}^{19}\frac{2^{k}}{k!} \approx 8.31 \times 10^{-6}\]

title: HW 2
text:
sol
step1 \(X,Y\)는 독립이므로 두 확률변수의 결합확률밀도함수를 다음과 같이 쓸 수 있음.
\[P\{X = i, X+Y=k\} = P\{X = i, Y=k-i\} = P(X = i)P(Y = k-i).\]
step2
\[P(X=i) = \binom{n}{i}p^{i}(1-p)^{n-i}, \quad P(Y=k-i)=\binom{m}{k-i}p^{k-i}(1-p)^{m-(k-i)}\]
step3
\[P(X = i, Y=k-i)=\binom{n}{i}\binom{m}{k-i}p^{k}(1-p)^{n+m-k}\]
step4 두 확률변수는 같은 \(p\)를 갖는 독립 이항분포를 따르므로
\[X + Y \sim \text{bin}(n+m,p)\]
\[\therefore\,\,  P(X=i|X+Y=k) = \frac{\binom{n}{i}\binom{m}{k-i}}{\binom{n+m}{k}} \]

title: HW 2
text:
(5) independent?
Are \(Y_1 - Y_2\) and \(Y_1 + Y_2\) independent?

sol.
\[U = Y_1+ Y_2,\,\,V = Y_1-Y_2\]
1 정규분포를 따르는 두 확률변수의 선형변환은 다시 정규분포를 따르므로 위 \((U,V)\)는 이변량 정규분포를 따른다.
2 공분산 계산

title: HW 2
text:
(6) The distribution of
\[\sum_{k=1}^{5} \frac{(Y_{2k-1}-Y_{2k})^2}{2\sigma^2}\]

sol
step1
\[D_{k} = Y_{2k-1} - Y_{2k} \sim N(0, 2\sigma^2)\]
step2
\[Z_{k} = \frac{D_{k}}{\sqrt {2}\sigma} \sim N(0,1)\]
\[Z_{k}^2 \sim \chi_{1}^{2}\]
step3
서로 독립인 카이제곱분포를 따르는 확률변수들의 가법성 성질을 이용하면!
\[\therefore \,\,T = \sum_{k=1}^{5} Z_{k}^2 = \sum_{k=1}^{5} \frac{(Y_{2k-1}-Y_{2k})^2}{2\sigma^2} \sim \chi^{2}_{5}\]
